response: Yes, p53 alterations can be used to predict tumor response to pre-operative chemo-radiotherapy in locally advanced rectal cancer. Studies have shown that tumors with mutated or altered p53 are more resistant to radiation and chemotherapy, and therefore may not respond as well to pre-operative chemo-radiotherapy. In contrast, tumors with wild-type p53 are more likely to respond to treatment. As a result, p53 status can be used as a biomarker to predict treatment response and guide treatment decisions in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer.
